title: fix(runtime): skip unsupported Node runtimes for helper processes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Node helper subprocesses selecting an unsupported system Node ahead of a supported installation when OpenClaw runs under Bun. In CI, Gateway post-ready maintenance launched Node 20.20.2 and failed to parse a compiled module's `using` declaration despite Node 24.22.1 being installed.

## User Impact

Node-only helpers select a runtime supported by OpenClaw. If none is available, the resolver returns `undefined` through its existing contract. PATH hardening, candidate order, required flags, and caller environment handling stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current-runtime fast path and standalone probe now use the existing canonical Node support predicate. The generated executable programs are regenerated through their owner. Existing resolver, generated-program, and child-process tests cover the behavior, and the SDK documentation describes the supported-runtime contract. Sparse CI and source-scanner fixtures retain the canonical version module required by the resolver.

## Evidence

- Real mixed-runtime reproduction in a qualified native checkout: the pinned Bun fork runs the existing Gateway post-ready `settles` case with official Node 20.20.2 ahead of supported Node in the test subprocess PATH. Before regeneration it fails on the same `using` syntax error; afterward the unchanged case passes. Results: 1 failed / 2 skipped before, 1 passed / 2 skipped after. Total wall times: 46.32s and 32.26s.
- Focused proof: 7 resolver cases, 5 generated-program cases, and 2 real child-process cases pass. Resolver suite wall time 0.339s; generated-program test bodies total 0.366s within a 5.10s combined run; child-process suite wall time 2.07s.
- Generated-output check, both affected test typecheck leaves, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Initial local review identified the stale generated programs; that correction is complete. Fresh full-range local review found no actionable correctness or security defects.
- Ordinary CI on the first prepared head exposed two missing-module failures in sparse/isolated harnesses. The actual existing planner and scanner cases reproduced 2 failures / 1 pass before the two inventory additions and pass all 3 afterward (6.16s → 4.72s). Scoped typecheck, lint, formatting, workflow validation, and diff checks pass; a fresh correction review found no actionable correctness or security defects.
- Corrected-head [CI43208880460](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43208880460) completed with 83 successful jobs, 21 skipped and four workload failures plus the aggregate gate. Security, CodeQL, OpenGrep and workflow checks passed. The scanner regression also passed in hosted CI (455ms).
- The remaining failures are retained under scoped maintainer source attribution: an upstream logger-worker fixture-graph mismatch, an upstream eager TLS import rejected by the existing help test, a fake Git missing the capability probe expected by the existing merge tests, and Docker prepublish packing of acorn@8.19.0. The Docker packing path and inputs are unchanged and do not invoke the changed resolver; its underlying npm error is unknown. No matching baseline execution or green CI is claimed. Final Boat qualification must still exercise the Docker payload.
- The original CI failure is retained. The four separate Gateway RPC timeouts are outside this fix; this local reproduction does not claim a complete Linux or Windows qualification.

The mixed-runtime command is the normal test owner with an isolated fixture PATH:

```sh
PATH="$NODE20_BIN:$PATH" OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH="$PINNED_BUN" \
  OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 \
  "$SUPPORTED_NODE" scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-server.config.ts \
  src/gateway/server-startup-post-ready.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 \
  -t 'holds post-ready maintenance until deferred startup settles'
```
